text: __NOTOC__ Nazz Steamboil was the pilot of the goblin racer in the Mirage Raceway. The Goblin Rumors said that he went into hiding after stealing a small fortune from his family's hoard. Nazzivus Monument Glyphs are located upon Nazzivus Monument in Nazzivian on Bloodmyst Isle.
Necrolords are humans found at Gjalerbron in the Howling Fjord.
Necro Overlord Mezhen is the necrolord in charge of awakening the vrykul at Gjalerbron. He can be found conducting a ritual on a captured prisoner. He fights with the regular shadow bolts.

This article outlines loot dropped in the dungeon Naxxramas. The loot in this dungeon was the best in the game until the Burning Crusade was released. Among the loot is the Tier 3 raid armor sets.

Naz'anak: The Forgotten Depths is a cave located far beneath Icecrown Citadel. It is divided into two small rooms, each with a small lake at their center. They are connected by a nerubian hallway that contains the Altar of the Ebon Depths. Naz'anak has a rich biodiversity of fungal plantlife, and also has faceless ones. Matthias Lehner could also be found here. Adventurers explored the cavern but the explosion of several saronite bombs knocked them off the rail, and into a large saronite-lined hole, falling down through a crack in the ice into the water.
Necklace of Arcane Spheres drop from Xevozz in the Violet Hold on heroic mode.

Necklace Repair is a jewelcrafting quest, requiring 375 skill and a single Chalcedony to complete. Other than completing the Dalaran jewelcrafting daily quests, and trading Titanium Powder for tokens, it is the only other source of Dalaran Jewelcrafter's Tokens.
Necklace of Fragmented Light is a quest reward from Disarmament.
The Nebula Band can be looted from the Gift of the Observer after defeating Algalon the Observer in the 10-man version of Ulduar.

Navy Swordsmen are an elite melee unit of Kul Tiras. They were among the first wave to commandeer Theramore Isle's defenses from Jaina for Daelin Proudmoore, and tried to capture Rexxar and his companions on the orders of the Lord-Admiral.
Navy Snipers are the elite ranged unit of the Kul Tiras army. They were among the first wave to commandeer Theramore Isle's defenses from Jaina for Daelin Proudmoore.
Naxxramas Worshippers are elite humans found in the Arachnid Quarter of Naxxramas, as part of the Grand Widow Faerlina encounter.
Naxxramas Followers are humans found in Naxxramas, as part of the Grand Widow Faerlina encounter in 25-player mode. They are best killed as soon as possible.
Neck-Deep in Vile (10 player) is a dungeon & raids achievement earned for killing every Vile Spirit that spawns before it explodes and then defeat the Lich King on 10-player mode.
Nazzivus Summoners are satyrs standing around the summoning circle in Nazzivian in Bloodmyst Isle. They summon Tzerak who immediately kills them with Hellfire.

Nazzivus (or the Nazzivian) is a sect of satyrs in the camp Nazzivian in Bloodmyst Isle. They built the Nazzivus Monument with glyphs on it telling how some Highborne night elves willingly became satyrs and servants of the Burning Legion. The satyr also summon the felguard Tzerak here who calls them weaklings and kills the summoners. As of the end of the Fourth War, the satyrs are of a limited threat, but not fully gone.
Nazgrim's Flare Gun is a quest item for Fire Is Always the Answer and The Final Blow!

The Naz'jar are a group of naga found at Throne of the Tides in Abyssal Maw and in Shimmering Expanse. They are led by Lady Naz'jar, whom they serve exclusively. They appear to be her personal forces.
Necklace of the Furious Standard is a quest reward from A Standard Day for Azrajar.
The Necklace with Elune Pendant is a common night elf archaeology artifact that requires 30 fragments to solve.
Naz'jar Honor Guards spawn during the Lady Naz'jar boss fight in Throne of the Tides. They are also seen in Shimmering Expanse and Abyssal Depths.
Naz'jar Tempest Witches spawn during the Lady Naz'jar boss fight in Throne of the Tides, and are also static mobs found in groups before reaching Lady Naz'jar.
Naz'jar Spiritmenders are naga located in the Throne of the Tides.

__NOTOC__ Nearly Headless Jacob is a master Pet Tamer located at the shore of the Mirror of Twilight in Crystalsong Forest. He is surrounded by his three level 25 battle pets: Stitch, Mort, and Spooky Strangler. Defeating him is required to complete the Taming Northrend achievement.

Neal Acree is a composer known for his work across film, television and video games. He has been creating music for World of Warcraft since The Burning Crusade. Neal is responsible for the cinematic music of the game as well as animated shorts such as Harbingers: Khadgar. Other game projects include Overwatch, StarCraft II, Diablo III and Heroes of the Storm, while Acree's screen credits include , , and more than 30 feature films as of 2016.
Nazargen is a doomguard located at the Thunder Axe Fortress in Desolace. He was summoned by the Burning Blade.

Navigator Taylor is a human located aboard the Alliance airship, controlled from the Hangar in Isle of Conquest.

Prior to the Battle for the Broken Shore, like many other followers, she appears in Stormwind Harbor at the sparring ring, where champions duel in preparation for the assault on the Broken Shore.

Nazra Wildaxe is a boss in Karazhan. She appears when Moroes accidentally opens the wrong portal. She appears to be a former member of the Old Horde as she knows Grommash Hellscream personally and is surprised that the Cho'gall is there, which could mean that she knows of their betrayal.

Naz'jar Serpent Guards are naga who guard the Ruins of Vashj'ir. In the visions of the Battlemaiden, they are at the Nar'shola Terrace probably commanding the Azsh'ir Soldiers.
Naz'jar Soldiers are naga located in the Throne of the Tides. They are fighting against Elemental Guards.

The Nazeshi are a group of naga operating in the Dreadpearl Shallows in Zuldazar. They originally arrived in a storm and then either allied or enslaved the Squallfin murlocs, after that capturing several of the local Tortollan Seekers. They were in a hurry to gather :Azerite for their queen at Covescale Rise. They were in communication with the Zanchuli Council. This happened before knowledge of Azerite became widespread in Zandalar. Later, they sent another expedition led by Tidecaller Nezara. This expedition was thwarted by Nisha's efforts.
The Nearly-hatching Pterrordax Egg is found in Tal'gurub in Zuldazar.

The Nazmani tribe is a tribe of blood trolls inhabiting Zul'Nazman in Nazmir. The Alliance also dealt with them. They seemed to be originally friendly and open to trade and fight against the Horde. Captain Conrad established a trust with the tribe, having been believed to be a messenger of G'huun. It was formerly a Zandalari tribe.

Nazmani Weevils are beetles located at Zul'Nazman in Nazmir, Uldir, and the Underrot. They also come in white and blue coloration.

Nazgrim's Axe is the formidable weapon of General Nazgrim. Nazgrim went down with the zeppelin and was feared dead; the axe is returned to him, and his injuries are revealed to have been non-life threatening.

Looting an item because you intend to use that item yourself, whether as equipment or for crafting purposes. This is an important distinction when looting with a party as it is considered polite to let those who need an item have it. Often abbreviated N or U in party conversation. Opposite of Greed.

Need Before Greed describes a rule of looting etiquette as well as a deprecated loot setting enforcing that etiquitte. While part of a party most players will expect that if they need an item they should get first pick at it before those who want it for Greed. For example, a party consisting of a rogue, a mage, and a warrior walk into a bar and loot some rare cloth armor. All of them can potentially wear that armor, but only the mage really needs it, the rest will likely just sell it or give it to an alt (see Greed). Therefore, it is expected that the warrior and rogue will allow the mage to have it by not rolling on the item.

in Ashenvale]] Neeloc Greedyfingers was a goblin merchant who Grommash Hellscream met while overseeing the harvesting of lumber from Ashenvale Forest. He offered to sell Grom his wares (including some goblin shredders which were capable of felling trees at a much faster rate than Grom's laborers) at cost if the chieftain would do him a favor. Greedyfingers explained that the bear-like furbolgs, who had been relatively harmless in the past, had been getting increasingly hostile and attacking him and the other goblins in his group. He wanted Grom to get rid of them. The Warsong chieftain took the deal and made good use of the shredders after slaying the furbolgs and their chieftain. Greedyfing

__NOTOC__ The Nek'mani Wellspring is a sacred spring located high in the cliffs overlooking the Southern Savage Coast on the west side of the Cape of Stranglethorn. Its Holy Spring dispenses the only clean freshwater south of Duskwood. The spring is the subject of great conflict among religious scholars, since every race in Azeroth claims that the waters were made divine for their people. An expedition of naga explorers have recently advanced on the spring and guard it ferociously.

His medallion is rumored to give an unnatural life span, for a price, that is. Thadius Grimshade wants Nekrum's medallion. Note that Nekrum is an undead target and can be hit with spells such as Shackle Undead, Holy Wrath, and Turn Undead. Seeing how Sharpbeak has escaped and is all grown up, it would imply that Nekrum was taken down.

Neeka Bloodscar is an orc quest giver located in the Horde watch tower at Splinterspear Junction in Swamp of Sorrows. She is one of the Horde's best trackers, trained in the Badlands. She could originally be found in Kargath in Badlands, as a battle-hardened and cynical scout. Since the Cataclysm, she was stationed at Splinterspear Junction to watch for Alliance activity. She is watching over her mate, Helgrum, who was fatally injured during in an Alliance attack.
__NOTOC__ Neii is a draenei tailoring vendor located at the Trader's Tier in the Exodar. During the Battle for the Exodar, she was inside Velen's protective shield, lying down.
Negaton Screamers are voidcallers that can be found in the Arcatraz.
Necromancer Leggings are a world drop from level 28 - 38 mobs.
Needle Threader is a bind on equip bow. Notably, before patch 7.0.3, it was the only bow in the game with spirit on it, an artifact from the times before patch 4.0.1, when hunters used mana.
The Necropile Robe drops from the following bosses in Scholomance: *The Ravenian *Doctor Theolen Krastinov *Lord Alexei Barov *Instructor Malicia *Lorekeeper Polkelt *Lady Illucia Barov
The Necropile Cuffs drop from the following bosses in Scholomance: *The Ravenian *Doctor Theolen Krastinov *Lord Alexei Barov *Instructor Malicia *Lorekeeper Polkelt *Lady Illucia Barov
The Necropile Boots drop from the following bosses in Scholomance: *The Ravenian *Doctor Theolen Krastinov *Lord Alexei Barov *Instructor Malicia *Lorekeeper Polkelt *Lady Illucia Barov
Necropile Leggings are cloth leggings which drop from bosses found in Scholomance.
The Necropile Mantle drops from the following bosses in Scholomance: *The Ravenian *Doctor Theolen Krastinov *Lord Alexei Barov *Instructor Malicia *Lorekeeper Polkelt *Lady Illucia Barov

Nemas the Arbiter was one of five ghostly paladins that spawned outside the Alonsus Chapel in Stratholme during the final part of True Masters of the Light (3), the charger quest for Blood Knights. He — along with his four compatriots, as well as Aurius the Chapel's "keeper" — must be defeated into order to complete the quest.
Neill Ramstein shows up with the Brewfest event, and helps out by teaching the public the finer points of ram racing.
Neeka's Report is provided as an objective for Report to Helgrum.

The necropolis serves as the central command structure of the undead army. Lumber harvested by ghouls is processed, and loyal acolytes train for tasks from their undead masters. Even when unattended, the vengeful spirits of the dead protect the necropolis from enemy attackers. In time, this structure can be further modified to become the Halls of the Dead. After that, it also may turn into a Black Citadel.
Necrotechs are humans located at Chillmere Coast in the Howling Fjord.
Nelno Copperbeam is the dockmaster of Valiance Keep in the Borean Tundra.

Killing undead mobs spawned around the shard will reduce its health. When the shard reaches around 1% health, it will turn into a Damaged Necrotic Shard (turning from green to blue) and 4 will spawn around the shard to begin channeling magenta energy streams into the shard. If you talk to the Cultist Engineers, you can trade to kill one and spawn an elite .

The Necrotic Vault is the final room of the Plague Quarter in Naxxramas. The fungal monster Loatheb, a foul experiment combining the Plague of Undeath with the bog beasts of Azeroth's swamps and marshes, is held within the Vault.
Necromantic Runes can be found throughout the Maw of Neltharion in Dragonblight.
Needy is a Legacy achievement earned for winning a need roll on a or better item above level 185 by rolling exactly 100.
__NOTOC__ Needle-Encrusted Scorpion drops from Devourer of Souls in the Heroic version of Forge of Souls.

Nefarian is the last boss of Blackwing Descent, a raid shipped with World of Warcraft: Cataclysm. He can be found in the Vault of the Shadowflame, where he resurrects his sister Onyxia, who makes up the first phase of the fight. Throughout the fight, Nefarian has several other undead adds as well.
Neeloc's Outpost was a shop just outside Orgrimmar in Durotar. It was presumably founded and ran by the goblin Neeloc Greedyfingers.
Neglected Footpads is a quest reward from Get Me Outta Here!
Needlerock Riders are stone troggs located at Stonehearth in Deepholm. They are trying to fight off the earthen and are mounted on Deadly Crystalgazers.

Needlerock Slag is the home of the stone trogg within Deepholm. The town is located just north of the Fractured Front and Stonehearth. The Earthen, which has been warring with the troggs for thousands of years, have brought the battle into their home after the troggs invaded Stonehearth and captured the Stonefather. The stone trogg mystics have control over the fungal giants that sprouted below and send them to attack the Earthen.
__NOTOC__ Needlerock Mystics are stone trogg casters located in Needlerock Slag in Deepholm.

Nefarian's Lair is, as the name implies, the throne of Nefarian, Lord of Blackrock Spire and the final boss of Blackwing Lair. It is the final named area in the raid, accessed upon the defeat of Chromaggus in the Crimson Laboratories. Upon arrival, the players will see Lord Victor Nefarius (the human guise of Nefarian) sitting upon his throne at the southeastern end of the room. Speaking to him will begin the encounter. It is also worth noting that from this area, one can see out across the Searing Gorge from a very high point of view; fortunately, there is an invisible wall designed to keep players from falling off the ledge.

Nell is a horse located at the final Plagues Grain Crate in the Culling of Stratholme wing of the Caverns of Time. He, Pepper and Bartleby Battson arrived in Stratholme after receiving a grain shipment from Andorhal. During the The Deaths of Chromie, it has been revealed that Pepper and Nell made their way inside Stratholme. The two horses ate the gain and soon turned into Risen Steeds.

Nekali is a jungle troll shaman trainer located at the Darkspear Training Grounds on the Darkspear Isle on the Echo Isles in Durotar. During the Burning Legion's third invasion, she joined the Earthen Ring and is seen in the Heart of Azeroth on the Maelstrom. She later traveled to Deliverance Point on the Broken Shore. When Zalazane returned, she defended the Darkspear Training Grounds.
Needles Pyrite Ore Chunk is contained in Needles Iron Pyrite in Thousand Needles.
__NOTOC__ Nelur Lightsown is a blood elf paladin trainer located at the Sunreaver's Sanctuary in Dalaran.

Neferset Insignias drop from the following tol'vir in Uldum: *Neferset Venom Keeper *Neferset Cursebringer *Neferset Ritualist *Neferset Snake Charmer *Neferset Armorer *Neferset Savage *Neferset Blade Twister *Neferset Raider *Neferset Scryer

These bombs have no fuse or other apparent triggering mechanism. They look like spheres made of iron, with only a single flat surface to keep them from rolling away if placed on even ground. Although these are usually referred to a "Neevil's bombs," Neevil himself denies ever inventing such a weapon. Instead of a fuse, the device detonates when it hears a pre-arranged detonation word. To prevent accidents, the word is not "programmed" into the bomb, but set by the owner just prior to use. The owner places the device where he wants it to be, puts his hand atop the smooth surface, and says "Activate Explosives" followed by the word he wants to invoke detonation. Neill Penny can be found outside the main building of Gallywix's Villa in Kezan, conversing with a couple Kezan Socialites. It's unknown if he survived.
Nedric Sallow is a Forsaken profession trainer located inside the inn of Brill in Tirisfal Glades.

Nectarbreeze Orchard is an orchard found in southwestern Jade Forest, just southwest of the Serpent's Heart. The farm has been producing nectar for generations, but is now under attack by the mogu from Camp Gormal via the hastily-created Splintered Path. They are attempting to burn down the farm and those that they do not kill get dragged off into the woods.
Needle Sprites are sprites located in groups of three at the Autumn Plains and Pranksters' Hollow in Kun-Lai Summit.
Nectarbreeze Farmers are pandaren farmers located at Nectarbreeze Orchard in the Jade Forest. They are attempting to defend the orchard from the Gormali clan.
The Nectarbreeze Cloak is a quest reward from What's Mined Is Yours.
